summary: Two authenticated Burn CPU/WASM workers returned the exact eight-tensor adapter trainable set, were accepted once, produced a restartable canonical adapter checkpoint with separate weight and full-state identities, and matched an independent centralized Python step with cosine similarity 0.9999999999985897.

guardrails.detail: Both browser results and the checkpoint contained exactly 8 declared adapter tensors and 8,192 values; base gradients were not accepted.
The accepted-work ledger retained exactly one entry for browser-a and one for browser-b over disjoint ranges.
Relative L2 against the independently generated centralized Python adapter checkpoint was 1.6795715402185043e-6.

After coordinator restart, status remained step_complete at optimizer step 1, the adapter endpoint returned SHA-256 ebae0d5fa8886ced1261e294465ee3be0c890b3c6271b82ad65a38ac6f947dc2, and the complete resume-state identity remained 9e621151601e7b28e51dc666f66b23ecaa58157b6cbdaef6977d7902bd2da29a.
All repository tests passed, including the existing dense coordinator, restart, HTTP, and browser-contract regressions.

findings.label: Connected adapter-only global step established
findings.description: The previously isolated browser LoRA path now completes authenticated leased assignments and contributes to a coordinator-owned canonical adapter checkpoint.

findings.label: Worker weights and full resume state remain distinct
findings.description: Assignments identify the immutable base, current adapter, combined worker-facing weight checkpoint, complete optimizer-backed resume state, and exact trainable set independently; workers are not coupled to coordinator-only optimizer moments.

findings.label: Split-batch FP32 rounding remains measurable
findings.description: Summing two independently executed two-row browser gradients yielded a checkpoint relative L2 of 1.6795715402185043e-6 versus one four-row Python pass, while remaining far inside the declared gate.

limitations: Both logical workers ran sequentially in one local headless Chrome instance and do not characterize heterogeneous community hardware or network behavior.
The complete frozen T0 base still resides in browser-accessible memory; LoRA reduces trainable state and upload size but does not prove base-model offload.
The synthetic one-step T0 fixture establishes numerical and persistence correctness, not useful adaptation quality.
Persistent multi-step LoRA campaign evaluation and release are not part of this experiment.
The experiment uses owner-approved local participants and does not qualify public untrusted compute.
